test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Usha Mehta is famously known for which of the following contributions during the Quit India Movement?

options.text: Leading armed struggle against British forces
Organizing the underground radio to broadcast nationalist messages
Being the first woman to be executed by the British for revolutionary activities

solution:
The correct answer is __**Organizing the underground radio to broadcast nationalist messages**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Usha Mehta** was a dedicated freedom fighter who gained national prominence during the **Quit India Movement** in **1942** for establishing the **Secret Congress Radio**, also known as **Azad Hindi Radio**. Hence, the statement about organizing the underground radio is correct.
 
• The underground station began its first broadcast on **August 14, 1942**, helping to spread the message of **Mahatma Gandhi** and other leaders after the **British Raj** arrested the top Congress leadership under **Operation Zero Hour**. Hence, her contribution was vital for maintaining communication among activists.
 
• To avoid detection by the **British authorities**, the radio transmitter was frequently moved between different hidden locations across **Bombay** (now Mumbai). The station operated on a frequency of **42.34 meters** and successfully bypassed strict colonial censorship for nearly three months. Hence, this clandestine activity provided a platform for uncensored nationalist news.
 
• **Usha Mehta** and her team, which included **Vithalbhai Jhaveri**, **Chandrakant Jhaveri**, and **Babubhai Thakkar**, were eventually betrayed and arrested by the police on **November 12, 1942**. Hence, her courageous efforts concluded with a period of rigorous imprisonment in **Yerawada Jail**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolutionary and Protest Contexts**:
 
 
• **Armed Struggle**: While groups like the **Indian National Army (INA)** led by **Subhas Chandra Bose** and the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** engaged in armed conflict, **Usha Mehta's** role was focused on non-violent but clandestine communication.
 
• **Execution of Women**: **Matangini Hazra** was a notable martyr of the **Quit India Movement** who was shot dead by British police while leading a procession, whereas **Pritilata Waddedar** is remembered for her revolutionary sacrifice during the **Chittagong Armoury Raid** of **1932**.
 
• **Mass Protests in Bombay**: **Aruna Asaf Ali** is the leader most famously associated with leading mass protests and hoisting the **Indian National Flag** at the **Gowalia Tank Maidan** in **Bombay** on **August 9, 1942**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Independence Recognition**:
 
 
• Following India's independence, **Usha Mehta** became a distinguished academic and was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1998** for her exceptional service to the nation.
